description: The full IMAX frame. Shot on 15/70 film cameras or IMAX-certified digital cameras. Only visible in IMAX GT Laser or 15/70 film venues — CoLa and dual-xenon digital IMAX max out at 1.90:1.
home_release_behavior: Cropped to 1.78:1 for home release — loses ~19.7% of vertical content. No consumer display standard can show the full 1.43:1 frame.

description: The standard IMAX digital frame for CoLa and dual-xenon IMAX venues. Taller than 16:9 but narrower than 1.43:1. Also used for IMAX Enhanced home releases.
home_release_behavior: Preserved on IMAX Enhanced certified displays. Cropped to 1.78:1 on standard 16:9 TVs, showing ~6.3% more than the 16:9 frame.

description: The standard widescreen cinema format. Used for most Hollywood blockbusters. The baseline for extra_area_vs_scope_pct calculations — all other formats are compared against this.
home_release_behavior: Displayed with thin letterbox bars on 16:9 TV. IMAX venues show scope at 1.90:1 max width — no extra height benefit.

description: The standard flat widescreen format. Near-full use of screen width on standard screens. Used for many dramas and comedies that don't shoot anamorphic.
home_release_behavior: Thin pillarbox bars on 16:9 TV. Near-full use of screen width.

description: The native aspect ratio of all 16:9 televisions and most streaming content. Fills the TV screen entirely. Wider than IMAX Digital (1.90:1) on a TV, but has far less total area than any cinema screen.
home_release_behavior: Fills the entire 16:9 TV screen. Wider than IMAX digital — but a TV is not a cinema.

description: 65mm large-format aspect ratio, also used for select Panavision productions. Notably used for Nolan dialogue sequences interspersed with 1.43:1 IMAX footage in films like Oppenheimer.
home_release_behavior: Letterboxed on 16:9 TV. Used for Nolan dialogue sequences interspersed with 1.43:1 IMAX footage.

description: Older anamorphic scope standard. Near-identical to 2.39:1 in practice; common in films from the 1970s–1990s and some contemporary productions using older optical standards.
home_release_behavior: Near-identical to 2.39:1 in practice; older anamorphic prints. Slight letterbox on 16:9 TV.
